subject: Kestrel pilot: requested uptime variance & remedies (executive approval)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cho <aaron@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service terms: uptime target & remedies for Kestrel pilot

Hi Aaron —

Great to meet yesterday. As discussed, the Kestrel pilot is a high-traffic workload (median 12k reqs/min with bursts) and they want a commercial package we can operate on shared capacity. They asked for two non-standard concessions we need to formalize:

1) Uptime SLO: allow 99.5% monthly uptime for the 6-month pilot (instead of our standard 99.95).
2) Remedies/cap: cap service credits at 10% of monthly invoice and reduce automatic restart/latency remedies to thresholds that match the pilot's tolerance.

Kestrel is also requesting a one-time 20% discount the first year if we accept the SLO variance. They'd sign quicker if we provide a short addendum rather than full contract redlines.

Can you confirm Redwood can accept these two items at a commercial level (discount + SLO variance)? If not, what escalation do you need? I've copied Marcus (deal owner) who will pull in legal/engineering approvals.

Best,
Aditya

Aditya —

Thanks, that summary is right. For clarity: the 99.5% uptime is only while we run the initial pilot (6 months). Kestrel Legal will send a short redline to the SLA addendum — they want the credit cap and the duration to be explicit and prefer DocuSign.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Please confirm there are no model-usage telemetry requirements beyond standard diagnostics. We want to avoid extra instrumentation work.
- If there's an operational mitigation fee for dedicated capacity during incidents, let us know so we can budget.

If you can get internal signoff this week, we can execute the addendum and kick off the pilot May 1.

Regards,
Aaron

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Service terms: uptime target & remedies for Kestrel pilot — exec approval request

Folks — forwarding the thread with Kestrel. They want two commercial exceptions for a 6-month pilot: 1) allow 99.5% monthly uptime (vs our standard 99.95) and 2) cap service credits at 10% of monthly invoice. They also asked for a 20% first-year discount.

Why I’m escalating: the SLO variance plus discount meaningfully increases our operational risk on shared pools. If we accept, engineering needs firm observability and rollback controls; legal needs a narrow addendum.

What I need from each of you by end of day:
- Evelyn: technical signoff on a limited SLO variance and the mitigation list we’d require (telemetry, incident runbooks, rollback triggers).
- Laura: legal approval on a short SLA addendum and required indemnities / SOC2 copy. Keep it narrow — we only want this for the pilot.
- Aditya: confirm commercial structure (monthly billing floor, contact at Kestrel).

Key commercial numbers for review:
- Requested discount: 20% Y1
- Proposed credit cap: 10% of monthly invoice
- Pilot duration: 6 months (start target May 1)

Attachments: I added the draft addendum Kestrel sent as an attachment (kestrel-sla-addendum_v1.docx).

Thanks — Marcus
---
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, North America Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Service terms: uptime target & remedies for Kestrel pilot — exec approval request

Marcus —

I can approve the technical exception under the following conditions (these are non-negotiable):
1) Timebox: the variance is limited to 6 months from the pilot start date; we revert to 99.95 afterward.
2) Observability: Kestrel must accept our standard telemetry markers for incident correlation (request IDs, timestamped error rates, percentile latency buckets). We will not require payload-level logging, but we do require traceability to customer requests.
3) Rollback/mitigation: if rolling 99.5% results in >3 Sev-2 incidents in a 30-day window tied to model throughput, we reserve the right to move the workload to dedicated capacity or suspend the pilot.
4) Reporting: weekly latency and error dashboards for the pilot duration (Redwood to push a shared dashboard view).

On credits: limiting caps to 10% is acceptable for the pilot, provided legal adds an explicit notice period and that credits don’t apply to customers for outages caused by customer misconfiguration.

I’ll coordinate with infra to stand up the dashboard and define the specific telemetry keys.

Evelyn

Subject: Re: Fwd: Service terms: uptime target & remedies for Kestrel pilot — legal redlines and next steps

Marcus / team —

I've reviewed Kestrel's proposed addendum and made the following high-level redlines (attached as kestrel-sla-addendum_v2.docx):
- Narrow the variance: explicitly state "pilot-only — 6 months" and include automatic reversion clause.
- Credit cap: accept 10% cap but add carve-outs where customer misconfiguration or third-party infra failures apply.
- Indemnity & liability: maintain standard liability cap (1x annual contract value) and add a short clause about cooperative incident response (timely access to logs/contacts).
- Compliance: require Kestrel provide a current SOC 2 attestation before execution.

I can sign off on this addendum once Evelyn confirms instrumentation is acceptable and Aditya confirms the commercial ask. I'll convert the addendum to DocuSign and share the link.

Next steps:
1) Evelyn confirms telemetry lines (done here).
2) Marcus confirms commercial numbers formally in the HubSpot deal (DEAL-8342).
3) I send DocuSign with kestrel-sla-addendum_v2.docx and pilot-mop.pdf attached.

Laura
